question: After successful wax removal, examination of the tympanic membrane is a mandatory step, because findings such as a perforation, tympanosclerosis, or retraction pocket identified at this point will directly influence subsequent management.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Inspecting the TM after wax removal is a mandatory final step, not optional. The cleared view may reveal a perforation that was previously hidden (changing the approach to any future ear procedures), tympanosclerosis, attic retraction, or cholesteatoma. Omitting this step is a clinical error.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Wax removal is not complete until the TM has been inspected. Asymptomatic perforations, tympanosclerosis, retraction pockets, or even cholesteatoma can be revealed once occluding wax is cleared. The management plan often changes significantly based on these findings.
